propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui beato Petro Apostolo tuo, collatis clavibus regni caelestis,
ligandi atque solvendi pontificium tradidisti: concede; ut, intercessionis
ejus auxilio, a peccatorum nostrorum nexibus liberemur: Qui vivis et regnas
cum Deo Patre in unitate.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Two pointers reach this text. Leaf n617, printed p. 609, heads 30 June `XXX. COMMEMORATION of St. PAUL.` and rubricates `All as on January 25, p. 543`; leaf n552, printed p. 544, then prints for 25 January `Of St. PETER, Deus, qui beato, as on the Feast of his Chair at Rome, the 18th of January, p. 538.` The oration itself stands on leaf n546, printed p. 538, with the Latin cue `Deus, qui beato.` The 1962 index reprints the same three orations under 01-25 and 06-30, and this file already records them at comm-s-petri-apostoli; the English is therefore recorded twice, as at the three commemorations named in the 1962 open_collation_items. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.
translations.source_label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)
translations.text: O God, who by delivering to the blessed apostle Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven, didst give him the power of binding and loosing: grant that, by his intercession, we may be freed from the bonds of our sins. Who livest.

commendet oratio: ut, quod pro illius gloria celebramus, nobis prosit ad
veniam. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et
regnat in unitate.

mirabilem praedicamus; sic per illum tuae sumamus indulgentiae largitatem.
Per Dominum.
